what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to name five members to a new cable advisory committee: two from the public access cable committee and three board members.
The board made the cable appointments without waiting for town counsel's answers on the committee.
The town manager said the governor's budget raises Chapter 70 and unrestricted aid above what the FY16 recommendation assumed, and includes an annual state payment that may not stay.
Health insurance renewal came in above the projection, and Monty Tech has not yet given a preliminary assessment, which is expected to be higher than budgeted.
Costs from four snow storms were submitted to FEMA as one event; the board and town manager indicated they would not use the governor's two-year amortization option.

why_it_matters: State aid, health insurance and the Monty Tech assessment all feed the FY16 budget, so each change moves the amount the town budget, mostly taxes, must cover.
Snow costs stay in FY16 rather than being spread over two years, and any FEMA reimbursement is not yet certain.
watch_next: The Monty Tech preliminary assessment, which had not yet been issued at this meeting.
Whether FEMA reimburses the snow costs, and whether a second annual state payment arrives and is directed to capital or one-time expenses.
